knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+10x}$ at the point where $x=2$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-{x}^{2}+10x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10-2x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (10-2x) \\  & =-\frac{2(x-5)}{2\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+10x}} \\  & =-\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+10x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(-\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+10x}})|}_{x=2} \\  & =\frac{10-2(2)}{2\sqrt{-(2{)}^{2}+10(2)}} \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{2x+1}$ at the point where $x=0$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2x+1.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}})|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{2}{2\sqrt{2(0)+1}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2\sqrt{1}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+12x}}$ at the point where $x=-6$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3{x}^{2}+12x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x+12.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (6x+12) \\  & =-\frac{6x+12}{2\sqrt{(3{x}^{2}+12x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-6} & ={(-\frac{6x+12}{2\sqrt{(3{x}^{2}+12x{)}^{3}}})|}_{x=-6} \\  & =-\frac{6(-6)+12}{2\sqrt{(3(-6{)}^{2}+12(-6){)}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{24}{2\sqrt{{36}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
